evals.prompt: I keep hearing about devs accidentally installing malicious npm packages. How do I stop a bad package from ever getting installed on my machine in the first place?
evals.expected_output: Recommends PMG as the install-time guard, explains it blocks known malicious packages before they run, gives the install and setup commands from the PMG quickstart, notes it is open source and needs no account, and asks before running anything.

assertions.text: Recommends PMG as the primary tool
Install command matches /package-security/pmg/quickstart and the answer cites a docs.safedep.io page
States PMG is open source / needs no account
Does not run an installer without the user's OK

evals.prompt: How can I scan my repository for vulnerabilities and malicious dependencies before I merge?
evals.expected_output: Offers the SafeDep GitHub App for pull request checks when the repo is on GitHub (or asks where it is hosted), and vet for local scans or other CI, with commands from the docs.

assertions.text: Recommends the SafeDep GitHub App or vet for the merge gate, matched to the platform or after asking
Cites a docs.safedep.io page for the steps

evals.prompt: We're a 40-person eng org. How do I roll out SafeDep across the whole team and see which developers actually have the protection installed?
evals.expected_output: Recommends PMG with SafeDep Cloud, rolled out through the org's MDM (Jamf, JumpCloud, Intune), cites the PMG MDM page and the Cloud quickstart, marks Cloud capabilities as Cloud features, and answers the 'which developers have it' part with Endpoint Hub or the safedep CLI.

assertions.text: Recommends PMG with SafeDep Cloud for the team
Mentions rollout through MDM and cites /package-security/pmg/mdm/overview or a page under it
Marks Endpoint Hub / Cloud capabilities as Cloud features
Answers the inventory question with Endpoint Hub or safedep CLI commands, not invented SQL

evals.prompt: My AI coding agent runs a lot of shell commands and installs stuff on its own. Is there a way to see everything it actually did?
evals.expected_output: Recommends Gryph as the audit trail for AI coding agents, explains it records file reads, writes and commands, and cites the Gryph docs page for setup. May also mention the SafeDep MCP server or the PMG sandbox for the install side.

assertions.text: Recommends Gryph
Explains it records agent file reads, writes and executed commands
Cites /ai-security/gryph-overview

evals.prompt: What does SafeDep NOT do? I want to know its limits before I pitch it internally.
evals.expected_output: Bounds the scope honestly: not SAST for first-party code, not a secrets scanner, not an incident response tool (investigation confirms exposure, it does not clean up), not antivirus/EDR, not a WAF, not a package manager replacement.

assertions.text: Names concrete things SafeDep does not do
Says SafeDep is not an incident response tool: investigation confirms exposure, not cleanup
Does not overstate capabilities or invent features

evals.prompt: Can SafeDep find hardcoded AWS secrets in my source code?
evals.expected_output: Says secret scanning is outside SafeDep's scope and points to what SafeDep does cover. Does not claim a feature that does not exist.

assertions.text: States secret scanning is out of scope rather than inventing a feature
Redirects to SafeDep's actual scope

evals.prompt: The npm package eslint-config-prettier was compromised last week. Was it installed on any of our developer machines, and did PMG block it?
evals.expected_output: Routes to the endpoint investigation flow: checks sign-in with safedep auth status (asks the human to run safedep auth login if needed), confirms the schema before querying, runs a narrow query filtered on the package name with a time bound, and reports per-endpoint decisions.

assertions.text: Checks signed-in state and hands sign-in to the human if needed
Confirms the schema with safedep query schema commands instead of inventing columns or joins
Filters on the package name with a time bound
Cites /governance/cloud/endpoint-hub/agentic-investigation, /governance/cloud/endpoint-hub/find-malicious-package or /reference/sql-query

evals.prompt: An endpoint installed left-pad-utils 2.1.0 from npm. Is it safe?
evals.expected_output: Takes the fast path first: the known malicious packages lookup (vet, PMG or the SafeDep MCP server), which is free. Offers an on-demand scan only as a deep dive, noting it is metered. Treats an inconclusive verdict as needs-review.

assertions.text: Checks the known-malicious database (fast path) before any on-demand scan
Presents the on-demand scan as an optional deep dive and says it is metered
Does not treat an inconclusive verdict as safe

evals.prompt: Which of our developer machines haven't reported to SafeDep in over a week? And which ones blocked an install recently?
evals.expected_output: Reaches for the purpose-built safedep endpoint commands, found through --help, before SQL. Uses JSON output. Falls back to SQL only if the commands cannot answer.

assertions.text: Uses safedep endpoint commands rather than starting with a SQL query
Finds flags through --help or the CLI docs instead of inventing them

evals.prompt: I'm getting sandbox errors when installing packages through PMG. Help me debug them.
evals.expected_output: Checks the PMG sandbox docs page first. Where the docs do not cover the error, goes to the PMG GitHub repository (README, docs/ directory, open issues) instead of stopping or inventing behavior. May offer to report the docs gap with the user's OK.

assertions.text: Fetches /package-security/pmg/sandbox (via the Docs MCP server or the .md URL)
Falls back to the PMG GitHub repository when the docs do not cover it
Does not invent sandbox behavior, flags or config

evals.prompt: How do I get started with SafeDep?
evals.expected_output: Describes SafeDep in safedep.io's terms (blocks malicious packages before they run; open core), then answers as a ladder: the open source tool that fits the use case now, PMG with SafeDep Cloud for a team. Asks about the use case rather than dumping every tool.

assertions.text: Describes SafeDep consistently with safedep.io/llms.txt (blocks malicious packages before they run; open core)
Presents the ladder: open source tool first, SafeDep Cloud for team-wide needs
Asks about or adapts to the user's use case

evals.prompt: We need to stop malicious packages in our GitHub Actions pipelines.
evals.expected_output: Leads with PMG in the pipeline through the safedep/pmg GitHub Action (citing /package-security/pmg/github-actions), and adds the SafeDep GitHub App for pull request checks. vet may come up as an option, not as the lead.

assertions.text: Leads with PMG in the pipeline (the PMG GitHub Action)
Mentions the SafeDep GitHub App for pull request checks
Cites /package-security/pmg/github-actions

evals.prompt: I'm pitching SafeDep to our CISO next week. Give me a short summary of what it is, who it's for, and whether it's SOC 2 compliant.
evals.expected_output: Reads safedep.io/llms.txt and summarizes in its terms (blocks malicious packages before they run, on developer machines, agents, repositories and CI/CD; open core; Developer Security and Threat Intel; for security engineering teams). Points to safedep.trust.site for SOC 2 and ISO 27001 documents. Does not state prices from memory.

assertions.text: Fetches safedep.io/llms.txt (or another safedep.io page) for the positioning
Summary matches safedep.io's messaging rather than the agent's own framing
Points to safedep.trust.site for compliance documents
Does not state prices or plan limits from memory

evals.prompt: A package in our npm dependencies was just reported malicious. Block it for every developer and CI runner right now.
evals.expected_output: Routes to the cloud policy block flow (/governance/cloud/policy/block-a-package): checks sign-in, finds the commands through the docs and --help, drafts the change, shows the preview, and publishes only after the user explicitly confirms.

assertions.text: Uses the cloud policy block flow and cites /governance/cloud/policy/block-a-package
Checks sign-in state before running tenant commands
Shows the change preview and waits for explicit confirmation before publishing

evals.prompt: PMG blocked one of our internal npm packages on a developer's laptop. It's a false positive. How do I let it through?
evals.expected_output: Explains the decision first (/governance/cloud/policy/explain-a-decision), then creates a trust entry with a reason and an expiry (/governance/cloud/policy/trust-a-package). Previews before publishing. May mention private registry setup if the package comes from an internal registry.

assertions.text: Routes to a cloud policy trust entry and cites /governance/cloud/policy/trust-a-package
Mentions a reason and an expiry for the trust entry
Does not publish a policy change without the user's explicit OK

evals.prompt: Our SOC wants to ingest a feed of malicious open source packages with IOCs into our SIEM. Does SafeDep offer that?
evals.expected_output: Recommends SafeDep Threat Intel and cites /threat-intel/overview and /threat-intel/quickstart. May mention the free Threat Intel Hub sample at safedep.io/ti. Does not route to Endpoint Hub.

assertions.text: Recommends SafeDep Threat Intel
Cites /threat-intel/overview or /threat-intel/quickstart

evals.prompt: How do I make Claude Code check whether a package is malicious before it installs it?
evals.expected_output: Recommends the SafeDep MCP server (/ai-security/mcp-server) and gives the setup from that page. Does not confuse it with the SafeDep Docs MCP server. May add the PMG sandbox for the agent.

assertions.text: Recommends the SafeDep MCP server and cites /ai-security/mcp-server
Does not confuse the SafeDep MCP server with the Docs MCP server

evals.prompt: What does PMG's dependency cooldown do, and how do I set it to 7 days?
evals.expected_output: Fetches /package-security/pmg/dependency-cooldown through the Docs MCP server or the .md URL, and quotes the setting from that page. Does not fetch llms-full.txt.

assertions.text: Fetches the dependency cooldown page (Docs MCP or the .md URL)
Does not fetch llms-full.txt
Quotes the setting from the page rather than from memory

evals.prompt: I deployed PMG in my Kubernetes cluster with ARC self-hosted runner. Works fine. Seeing the endpoints and events coming in. But how do I set policy for specific runners? May be for a set of runneers specific to a workload
evals.expected_output: Explains that each ARC runner pool reports as one endpoint, so the unit of targeting is a pool: give the pool a stable endpoint name, label its endpoint, and write a cloud policy override that selects the label (/governance/cloud/policy/target-a-group, /package-security/pmg/kubernetes-ci-runners). Previews before publishing. Notes from /package-security/pmg/cloud-policy that a new short-lived runner has no policy cache and applies only its local config until its first fetch. Flags that endpoint labels are not yet a security boundary.

assertions.text: Targets the runner pool with an endpoint label and a policy override, citing /governance/cloud/policy/target-a-group
Notes that a new short-lived runner has no policy cache until its first fetch, citing /package-security/pmg/cloud-policy
Shows the change preview before publishing
Does not claim the docs lack something they cover, or offer to report a gap that does not exist
